sentences.text: Shri Naveen Dubey - Government Advocate for the respon

Shri Manohar Chouhan, Sub Inspector posted in Police Station Civil Lines, Vidisha is present along with case diary of crime no. 382/04 which was registered at Police Station Dehat, District Vidisha for offence under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of IPC.

From the case diary it appears that a Khatma report was prepared which was rejected by the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha by his note dated 14.1.2007 and a direction was given to M-3 (C.S.P.) Vidisha to personally investigate the matter as offence under P. C. Act is also made out.
Thereafter, according to Shri Manohar Chouhan, diary was never opened by then C.S.P., District Vidisha.

Diary contains a letter dated 25.6.2012 written by then C.S.P., Vidisha bearing letter No.
N.PuA/Vidisha/Reader/8884/12, mentioning that prima facie no case under Prevention of Corruption Act is made out and acordingly, permission was sought from the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha for deleting offence under Section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

It is submitted by Shri Manohar Chouhan that after the offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act was deleted, the case diary was sent back to the police station and it appears that it remained pending without any attention.
Since Shri Manohar Chouhan is not the investigating officer, therefore, any submission made by him is not taken as an official statement.

However, one thing is clear that letter dated 25.6.2012 was never sent by C.S.P. Vidisha to Superintendent of Police, Vidisha for deletion of offence under Section 13 (1)
(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act because the case diary contains the original letter with original signature and original dispatch number and there is no endorsement by the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha thereby permitting to delete offence under Section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is clear that after the matter was handed over to C.S.P., Vidisha by the then Superintendent of Police, Vidisha by his note dated 14.1.2007 the diary was never opened and on one fine morning without doing anything, the C.S.P. Vidisha sought permission from the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha to delete the offence under Section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and kept the said letter in the diary itself.
Thereafter, the matter again went in hibernation and saw the light of the day only when this court vide order dated 9.10.2023 directed the Police Authorities to produce the case diary.

Since Shri Manohar Chouhan has seen the case diary, therefore, for the purposes of taking his assistance, a question was put to him as to whether any investigation was done after 14.1.2007 by any of the authorities or not ?.
It is fairly conceded by Shri Chouhan that after going through the case diary, he does not find even a single proceeding which may indicate that any investigation was done.

It is really surprising that the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha by his note dated 14.1.2007 had given a finding that prima facie it appears that an offence under Prevention of Corruption Act is made out and the closure report proposed by C.S.P. Vidisha on 13.1.2007 was also rejected by him but the subordinate staff of Superintendent of Police, Vidisha in utter disregard to the direction given by the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha, sat over the matter very conveniently as a result more than 16 years have passed and the diary did not see the light of the day.

As already pointed out, since Shri Chouhan is not the investigating officer, therefore, any of his statement is not being taken as an official statement but in the opinion of Shri Chouhan, it appears that diary remained pending in the police station.

It appears that Shri Chouhan made a statement with an intention to create an impression in the mind of the Court that without any fault on the part of any officer, the diary remained in police station in an unattended condition.

Accordingly, Shri Naveen Dubey, was directed to address this Court with regard to procedure as provided in the police regulation and which is to be adopted in the police station with regard to pending investigation.
It is fairly conceded by Shri Dubey that the moment an FIR is registered, an entry is made in Jarayan register and details of the pending investigation is recorded therein.

It is fairly conceded that in every monthly crime control meeting summoned by the Superintendent of Police,
C.S.P./D.S.P. as the case may be and the S.H.O. of the concerning Police Stations are under obligation to apprise the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha with regard to progress in all the pending investigations.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the case diary remained unattended in the police station without there being any malafides on the part of any police officer.

Thus, it is clear that either C.S.P./D.S.P. and S.H.O. of the concerning police stations were constantly informing the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha about the pendency of the investigation and even then the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha did not take any pain to get the investigation completed as the earliest or the then C.S.P./D.S.P. or the S.H.O. of the concerning police stations were not informing the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha at all about the pendency of this investigation.

If the second possibility is accepted then it is clear that even during the inspection of the police station the higher officials did not take pains to even go through Jarayan register,
otherwise they could have easily pointed out to S.H.O. of the concerning police station about the pendency of the investigation.

Therefore, it is clear that the Police Officers of the Police station Vishram Singh Bhadoriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124878117/

sentences.text: Be that whatever it may be.
It is the matter of investigation.

Accordingly, the Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh is directed to personally enquire into the matter and fix the liability of the officers who were / are responsible for conveniently sitting over the investigation including the C.S.P. having jurisdiction over Police Station Dehat, district Vidisha / Civil Lines, Vidisha;
S.H.O. of the concerning police station; Investigating officer of crime no. 382/04 as well as Superintendent of Police, Vidisha.

Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh shall seize the minutes of every monthly meeting of crime control presided over by the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha and shall point out as to whether the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha was ever informed about the pendency of this investigation or not.

Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh is also directed to seize all these inspection notes of the police station to find out as to whether the officer who had inspected the police station had ever noticed the pendency of the crime no.382/04 or not?.

Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh is also directed to give specific finding as to why the letter dated 25.6.2012 purportedly written by C.S.P. Vidisha was not actually sent to the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha for deletion of offence under Section 13 (1) (d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh is also directed to submit his report as to how C.S.P., Vidisha could give an opinion that no offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act is prima facie made out specifically when the Superintendent of Police, Vidisha was of the view that prima facie the offence is made out and the opinion formed by the C.S.P. Vidisha was not based on any subsequent evidence collected by him.
Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh is also directed to take necessary action against erring officers and submit his report.

Reader is also directed to seal the case diary and accordingly, in the presence of counsel for the petitioner, counsel for the State and in the presence of Shri Manohar Chouhan the case diary was sealed in the open Court.

It is made clear that entire inquiry shall be conducted by the Director General of Police by himself and he shall not assign this duty to any officer of any rank and he shall submit the report under his own signatures.
In view of the forth coming State Assembly Election and with a clear understanding that Director General of Police, State of Madhya Pradesh will be held up in maintaining law and order situation during this period
, therefore, report must be submitted on or before 15.2.2024.
